thread:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a quant + routing sweep on the new saffron-lite candidate vs our baseline chat workload. put a short summary below and a proposed traffic-split canary for product/GTN to review. TL;DR: 7b-int4 is ~2.3x cheaper with a small drop on long-form coherence slices; 13b-int8 recovers most quality at ~1.9x cost of 7b-int4.

alex: raw numbers from the slice sweep (chat benchmark, aggregated across 10k prompts):
```
Model            | P50 latency | P95 latency | tokens/sec | helpful_score_delta | halluc_rate_delta | cost per 1M tokens (hosted)
7b-int4          | 110ms       | 420ms       | 2300       | -1.2%               | +0.6%             | $9.5
13b-int8         | 145ms       | 500ms       | 1800       | -0.3%               | +0.1%             | $18.0
13b-fp16 (baseline)| 160ms     | 520ms       | 1700       | 0.0%                | 0.0%              | $42.5
```
Note: helpful_score is synthetic composite (answer relevance + instruction-following). halluc_rate measured on factual slices.

ravi: quick interpretation — unit economics: using our hosted pricing, switching new low-tier customers to 7b-int4 would cut token cost ~55–60% vs baseline 13b-fp16 but we'd expect a small signal loss on long-form recall. 13b-int8 looks like the sweet spot if product wants near-baseline quality with ~57% cost reduction vs fp16.

sam_gtn: from GTN perspective we care about two things: maintaining perceived parity for high-visibility flows (signup flows, onboarding help docs) and having a clear upsell path. if 13b-int8 is within 0.5% of baseline on our gated slices, we can position it as "premium accuracy" and route most free/plans to 7b-int4 while reserving 13b-int8 for paid tiers.

eval-bot: small automated check -> running slice regressions on top-10 user queries: 7b-int4 shows regression concentrated on "long-form multi-step reasoning" (slices: multi-step-recall, code-generation context). 13b-int8 passes 8/10 slices within ±0.4% of baseline.

maya: proposal for rollout/canary: start with 2% traffic to 13b-int8 (control traffic stays on fp16 baseline), 10% to 7b-int4, monitor these signals for 48h: helpful_score, halluc_rate, latency P95, and product conversion on onboarding flow. if no regression >1.0% on gated slices and latency SLOs OK, scale to 20%/60% split over 72h.

alex: sample canary routing config we can push to runtime (pseudo-config):
```
{
  "canary": {
    "duration_hours": 72,
    "initial_split": {"fp16": 0.88, "13b-int8": 0.02, "7b-int4": 0.10},
    "ramp_policy": "time_based",
    "checks": ["helpful_score", "halluc_rate", "p95_latency"],
    "rollback_condition": "any_check_drop > 1.0% on gated_slices"
  }
}
```
This will let us see isolated performance for both quant variants while keeping baseline healthy.

ravi: ops note — for Dedicated customers we should surface a clear toggle (route_by_customer_tier) so enterprise tenants can pin to 13b-int8 or fp16 if they want. also add a warm KV-cache priming pass for 13b-int8 to avoid cold-start tail.

sam_gtn: marketing/GTN asks — can we produce 2 short bullet points for the GTM page? suggestion:
- "Low-cost variant: Saffron-7b (INT4) — 2.3x cheaper for conversational workloads, ideal for free and entry tiers; small quality tradeoffs on long-form tasks."
- "Premium variant: Saffron-13b (INT8) — near-baseline quality at ~2x lower unit cost than fp16; recommended default for paid plans and high-visibility flows."

maya: decision so far: go ahead with the 2%/10% canary, alex to open canary PR and ops to prepare rollback playbook. product/GTM will draft messaging and pricing tiers.

alex: opened PR -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/inference/canary/1765009876 (deploy-bot will post status).

deploy-bot: canary job started: canary_id=canary-1765009876, started_at=2025-09-18T07:04:36Z

eval-bot: running checkpoints -> 6h check: 13b-int8 helpful_score_delta = -0.15% (within tolerance), 7b-int4 helpful_score_delta = -1.18% (expected); halluc_rate changes within thresholds. p95 latency stable under SLO.

sam_gtn: ok — looks safe for gradual ramp. product to confirm pricing notes and add a short experimental badge in the console so early adopters know their traffic might hit cheaper variants. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks all — I'll put a one-pager for PM/GTN with the numbers and the recommended routing tiers (attach to the canary PR). we'll reconvene if any slice crosses rollback thresholds.

alex: later note — we should add a small prompt-instruction tweak for the long-form slice when routed to 7b-int4 (2 tokens prefix reminding for stepwise decomposition). preliminary tests show that recovers ~0.6% helpful_score for long-form while adding negligible token cost.

maya: nice — add that to the A/B plan as an experiment.

ravi: filing a tiny ops TODO: create dashboard with these panels -> helpful_score (by slice), halluc_rate (by slice), p95 latency, cost burn per minute. link in PR.

maya: end-of-thread summary: recommended canary -> initial split 88% baseline / 2% 13b-int8 / 10% 7b-int4; success criteria -> no gated slice regression >1.0% and p95 latency within SLO. long-term recs -> default low-tier to 7b-int4 with prompt tweak, premium to 13b-int8, enterprise opt-in to fp16. thanks everyone. :rocket:
